triage.title: Triage
triage.description: Triage is the intake layer of the Software Factory. Incoming requests are reviewed, actionable engineering work is identified, duplicate items are checked, and the right work is routed to the right team before it reaches planning.
triage.panelDescription: These automations were created from the triage template and matched by their persisted template id. Each one turns inbound requests into structured work, preserves source context, and keeps duplicate items from fragmenting backlog ownership.

codeValidation.title: Validate
codeValidation.description: Validate is the quality gate before merge. Automated review, security, and QA workflows attach to repositories so implementation work is checked for correctness, risk, and expected behavior before it ships.

codeReview.title: Code review
codeReview.description: Pull requests are reviewed for correctness, regressions, maintainability, and repository-specific conventions. Focused feedback helps teams catch issues while context is fresh.

securityReview.title: Security review
securityReview.description: Adds a security-focused pass for vulnerabilities, secret exposure, unsafe dependencies, and security-sensitive code paths. Use it on repositories where changes need extra scrutiny before they merge.

qa.title: QA
qa.description: Plans validation around the changed behavior, runs the configured workflow, and reports failures with reproduction context. QA keeps implementation sessions tied to evidence that the user path still works.

securityAudit.title: Security audit
securityAudit.description: Runs a scheduled deep security review across the repository, surfacing vulnerabilities, secret exposure, and risky dependencies on a recurring cadence rather than per pull request.

docs.title: Document
docs.description: Document is the knowledge layer after code changes land. Repository documentation, setup steps, APIs, and architecture context stay aligned so engineers and agents can rely on the latest implementation map.

autoWiki.description: Reads the latest repository state and updates project knowledge with architecture notes, APIs, setup steps, and operational context. AutoWiki helps documentation stay close to the code instead of drifting over time.

observability.title: Monitor
observability.description: Monitor closes the loop between errors, incidents, and engineering action. Incident response automations organize follow-up work, while Agent Effectiveness checks whether automation activity is producing useful engineering outcomes.

incidentResponse.title: Incident Response
incidentResponse.description: Helps coordinate follow-up for incidents, errors, and alerts by gathering context, summarizing what changed, and tracking next steps. Use it to turn operational issues into structured engineering work.

agentEffectiveness.title: Agent Effectiveness
agentEffectiveness.description: Checks whether recent automation activity has been measured against engineering outcomes. This gives teams a simple signal that agent work is being evaluated, not just counted.
agentEffectiveness.recentRunDetected: A qualifying agent effectiveness run was detected in the last week.
agentEffectiveness.noRecentRunDetected: No qualifying agent effectiveness run was detected in the last week.

codeGen.title: Code-gen
codeGen.description: Code-gen is where engineering intent turns into implementation work. Connect your planning and communication systems so requests can be delegated with requirements, decisions, and repository context carried into the session.

slack.description: Delegate implementation work from a connected conversation. The surrounding discussion, files, and decisions become context for a session that reports progress back to the source.

linear.description: Delegate implementation work from a connected ticket. Issue details, comments, labels, and acceptance criteria become context while progress stays tied back to the source item.

modeCreateHelperText.qa: Clicking Create will open a new Droid session pre-filled with the /install-qa command and your selections above. The agent will analyze the selected repository interactively and generate the QA skill plus a .github/workflows/qa.yml workflow you can commit.
modeCreateHelperText.wiki: Clicking Create will open a pull request adding .github/workflows/droid-wiki-refresh.yml to the selected repository. The workflow refreshes the Factory Wiki on the trigger you selected (with your settings above) and can also be run manually. Each refresh also commits the wiki to the factory/droid-wiki branch and keeps a single pull request open with the latest version.
modeCreateHelperText.securityAudit: Clicking Create will open a pull request adding .github/workflows/deep-security-review.yml to the selected repository. The workflow runs /security-review across the codebase on your schedule (with your settings above) and can also be run manually.
modeCreateHelperText.codeWalkthrough: Clicking Create will open a pull request adding .github/workflows/droid-code-walkthrough.yml to the selected repository. The workflow generates a code walkthrough when a pull request is opened or marked ready for review, and updates it on every new commit. Walkthroughs are for pull requests reviewed in Factory's desktop and web app. The repository needs a FACTORY_API_KEY Actions secret.
modeCreateHelperText.codeWalkthroughWithoutUpdates: Clicking Create will open a pull request adding .github/workflows/droid-code-walkthrough.yml to the selected repository. wiki.description: Refresh a codebase wiki for your repository on a daily schedule and keep it in a rolling pull request.

securityAudit.name: Security Audit
securityAudit.description: Run a scheduled deep security review across your repository.

codeWalkthrough.name: Code Walkthrough
codeWalkthrough.description: Keep walkthroughs current for pull requests reviewed in Factory's desktop and web app.

triage.name: Triage
triage.description: Triage on a schedule and act on what needs attention.

incidentResponse.name: Incident Response
incidentResponse.description: Triage and run root-cause analysis on incidents.
incidentResponse.detailedDescription: It monitors your Slack alert channels. By default, it triggers on bot-authored alert messages posted to the channel and runs an RCA on the incident.

connectorPurposes.slack: Watches your alert channels and posts the RCA in the thread.

prBabysitter.name: PR Babysitter
prBabysitter.description: Watch your open pull requests on a schedule and drive failing CI to all-green.

slack.name: Slack
slack.description: Trigger Droid sessions from messages in Slack channels.

scheduled.name: Scheduled
scheduled.description: Run a prompt on a recurring schedule.

github.name: GitHub
github.description: Configure a custom GitHub Actions workflow that runs Droid on repository events.

webhook.name: Webhook
webhook.description: Trigger runs from any external service that can send an HTTP webhook.

chained.name: Automation-triggered
chained.description: Runs when a run of another automation ends. Pick which automations trigger it.

ticketToPr.name: Ticket to PR
ticketToPr.description: Pick up ready tickets from your tracker one at a time and drive each to an open pull request.

connectorPurposes.linear: Picks up ready tickets and links each one to its pull request.

prReviewer.name: PR Reviewer (GitLab/GitHub)
prReviewer.description: Review new pull or merge requests on a schedule and post one comment review per head commit. Works with GitLab as well as GitHub.

connectorPurposes.github: Reads new pull requests and posts one review per head commit.

dailyStatusDigest.name: Daily Status Digest
dailyStatusDigest.description: A morning digest of your PRs and tickets: what needs your action, what is waiting on others, and what moved since yesterday.

connectorPurposes.slack: Sends the morning digest to you.
connectorPurposes.linear: Reads the tickets assigned to you and what moved.
connectorPurposes.github: Reads your open pull requests and pending reviews.

codeHealth.name: Code Health
codeHealth.description: Rotate through dependency audits, dead code, coverage gaps, and stale docs, landing one small maintenance PR per run.

meetingNotesSync.name: Meeting Notes Sync
meetingNotesSync.description: Summarize finished meetings, extract action items, and file them into Notion, your CRM, or your tracker.

connectorPurposes.granola: Reads the notes from each finished meeting.
connectorPurposes.notion: Files the summary and action items.

errorTriage.name: Scheduled Error Triage
errorTriage.description: Poll Sentry, Datadog, or another error source hourly, investigate the errors that matter, and report root causes with a fix PR when safe.

connectorPurposes.sentry: Polls for new errors to investigate each hour.

slackDigest.name: Slack Digest
slackDigest.description: A private morning DM listing the Slack threads waiting on you, mentions to know about, and highlights from your channels.

connectorPurposes.slack: Reads DMs, mentions, and channel activity. Posts DMs to you.

slackBugFixer.name: Slack Bug Fixer
slackBugFixer.description: Turn bug reports posted in a channel into tickets, a root-cause hypothesis in the thread, and a fix PR when the change is small.

connectorPurposes.slack: Watches your bug-report channels and replies in the thread.
connectorPurposes.linear: Creates a ticket for each bug and links the fix.

channelQa.name: Channel Q&A
channelQa.description: Answer questions in a channel from your docs, Notion, tickets, and code, always citing sources in the thread.

connectorPurposes.slack: Watches your channel and answers in the thread.
connectorPurposes.notion: Searches your docs for the answer.

slackTicketFiler.name: Slack Ticket Filer
slackTicketFiler.description: File actionable channel messages as tickets, deduplicated and routed to the right team, with the link posted back in the thread.

connectorPurposes.slack: Watches your channel and posts the ticket link in the thread.
connectorPurposes.linear: Files each actionable message as a ticket.

alertResponder.name: Webhook Alert Responder
alertResponder.description: Investigate Sentry, Datadog, or PagerDuty alerts as they fire: root-cause analysis and a fix PR when safe. Runs on a Droid Computer or execution template. After saving, add the webhook URL to the sending service.

ciFailureTriage.name: CI Failure Triage
ciFailureTriage.description: Classify failed GitHub Actions or GitLab pipelines as flaky, infrastructure, or regression, and name the commit responsible. Runs on a Droid Computer or execution template. After saving, add the webhook URL to the sending service.

connectorPurposes.github: Reads the failed run and the commits behind it.

newIssueInvestigator.name: New Issue Investigator
newIssueInvestigator.description: Investigate each new Linear, Jira, or GitHub issue: duplicates, likely cause, files involved, and a PR for trivial fixes. Runs on a Droid Computer or execution template. After saving, add the webhook URL to the sending service.

connectorPurposes.linear: Reads each new issue and comments with what it found.

reviewCommentFixer.name: Review Comment Fixer
reviewCommentFixer.description: When a teammate comments on a pull request asking for a change, make it, push one commit to the branch, and reply.

testCoverage.name: Test Coverage
testCoverage.description: Add focused tests for the code each pull request changes, pushed to the branch with a comment on what is now covered.

docsRefresh.name: Docs Refresh
docsRefresh.description: Keep the docs in your repo current with each push to the default branch, via a pull request. For the Factory wiki, use AutoWiki.

useCases.title: Popular use cases
useCases.description: Jobs teams automate most, with the prompt and trigger filled in. Point one at your repositories and channels, then turn it on.

guidedSetups.title: Guided setups
guidedSetups.description: Built-in automations with a setup form tailored to the job.

blank.title: Start from scratch
blank.description: Pick a trigger and write the prompt yourself.

createWithDroidSuggestions.mergedPrDigest: Every weekday at 9am, summarize the pull requests merged yesterday and post the digest to #eng-updates.
createWithDroidSuggestions.sentryFix: When Sentry reports a new error, find the likely cause and open a draft pull request with a fix.
createWithDroidSuggestions.dependencyAdvisories: Every Monday, check our dependencies for security advisories and open pull requests to upgrade the affected ones.

triageDefaults.scanChannelsPlaceholder: e.g. all channels beginning with "engineering-", plus #customers and #bugs
triageDefaults.ticketGuidancePlaceholder: How should Droid file tickets? e.g. routing rules ("bugs about billing -> Payments team"), and which labels to attach.

prBabysitterDefaults.prFilterPlaceholder: Describe which PRs to watch, e.g. "PRs authored by me", "PRs where I'm requested as reviewer", or "every open PR in the repo".
prBabysitterDefaults.additionalInstructionsPlaceholder: Anything else Droid should know? e.g. checks that are known-flaky, or types of fixes to never auto-push.

constants.createAutomationSessionPrefill: Create an automation with Factory. Give me a quick explanation of how automations work, covering both triggers: a schedule runs the prompt on a cadence, and a webhook runs it whenever an external service POSTs to a receiver URL that is minted for the automation. Then ask what I want run and what should trigger it.

createWithDroidPrompt.openingNamed: Create an automation with Factory named "{{name}}".
createWithDroidPrompt.guidance: Before you create it, ask me for anything you still need, including what should trigger it: a schedule runs the prompt on a cadence, and a webhook runs it whenever an external service POSTs to a receiver URL that is minted for the automation.
